content: 1. Dryden-Peterson et al. (2015): The initial implementation of the WHO Option B program in Botswana was associated with an increase in projected mother-to-child transmission (MTCT) of HIV. This study was published in the Journal of Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndromes. 2. Egger et al. (1997): A simple graphical test was used to detect bias in meta-analyses, as detailed in the British Medical Journal. 3. Gartland et al. (2013): The field effectiveness of combination antiretroviral prophylaxis for preventing mother-to-child HIV transmission in rural Zambia was evaluated, showing promising results. This was published in AIDS. 4. Giuliano et al. (2013): Maternal antiretroviral therapy in Malawi was studied for its impact on maternal and infant outcomes two years post-delivery. The findings were published in PLOS One. 5. GRADEpro (2008): The GRADE Working Group developed a computer program to assist in creating evidence profiles and summary tables for clinical guidelines. 6. Guyatt et al. (2011, 2013a, 2013b): The GRADE guidelines were introduced to prepare evidence profiles and summary tables for binary and continuous outcomes, as published in the Journal of Clinical Epidemiology. 7. Herce et al. (2015): The scale-up of Option B+ and comprehensive PMTCT service delivery in Central Malawi was presented at the Conference on Retroviruses and Opportunistic Infections (CROI). 8. Higgins and Green (2008): The Cochrane Handbook for Systematic Reviews of Interventions provided guidance on conducting systematic reviews. 9. Hoffman et al. (2013): Biomarkers of inflammation and coagulation were studied in HIV-infected women who continued or discontinued antiretroviral therapy postpartum, as published in the Journal of Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndromes. 10. Kamuyango et al. (2014): A retrospective chart review in Malawi assessed one-year outcomes of women who started antiretroviral therapy during pregnancy before and after the implementation of Option B+. 11. Kesho Bora Study Group (2011, 2012): Randomized controlled trials compared triple antiretroviral prophylaxis with zidovudine and single-dose nevirapine during pregnancy and breastfeeding for preventing MTCT of HIV. The studies highlighted reduced transmission rates and maternal disease progression. 12. Kim et al. (2015): The impact of Option B+ on the antenatal PMTCT cascade in Lilongwe, Malawi, was evaluated, showing improvements in service delivery. 13. Kieffer et al. (2014): Lessons from the early implementation of Option B+ in 11 African countries were shared, emphasizing the experience of the Elizabeth Glaser Pediatric AIDS Foundation. 14. Liotta et al. (2013): A study in Malawi and Mozambique demonstrated a reduction in maternal mortality with highly active antiretroviral therapy in HIV-infected pregnant women. 15. Lu et al. (2015): Retention rates among HIV-infected pregnant women initiating lifelong antiretroviral treatment (Option B+) in Haiti were presented at CROI. 16. Minnear et al. (2013): Outcomes of women in Kenya who discontinued maternal triple-antiretroviral regimens used for PMTCT during pregnancy and breastfeeding were analyzed. 17. Mushabe et al. (2014): Integration of PMTCT Option B+ delivery with facility-level healthcare services in rural Uganda was discussed at the International AIDS Conference. 18. Namukwaya et al. (2013): Challenges faced by HIV-infected mothers in Uganda who refused to take up Option B+ drugs were shared at the International AIDS Society Conference. 19. Ngemu et al. (2014): The effectiveness of Option B highly active antiretroviral therapy (HAART) for PMTCT in pregnant HIV-positive women was evaluated in a study published in BMC Research Notes. 20. Nyandiko et al. (2010): Outcomes of HIV-exposed children in resource-constrained settings in Kenya were assessed, focusing on the efficacy of PMTCT interventions. 21. Okonji et al. (2012): CD4 and viral load responses, as well as adherence among breastfeeding women receiving triple antiretroviral prophylaxis for PMTCT in Kenya, were studied. 22. Palombi et al. (2014): The viro-immunological response and emergence of resistance in HIV-infected women receiving combination antiretroviral regimens for PMTCT in Malawi were analyzed. 23. Pai et al. (2006): Structured treatment interruptions in chronic unsuppressed HIV infection in adults were reviewed in the Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews. 24. Phillips et al. (2014): Disengagement from antiretroviral therapy services among HIV-positive pregnant and postpartum women in South Africa was studied, highlighting retention challenges. 25. Price et al. (2014): Uptake of PMTCT using Option B+ in rural Malawi was evaluated in a retrospective cohort study. 26. Shapiro et al. (2010, 2013): Antiretroviral regimens during pregnancy and breastfeeding in Botswana were studied, focusing on maternal mortality, CD4 counts, and infant HIV transmission. 27. Speight et al. (2013): The implementation of Option B+ for PMTCT at Bwaila Maternity Unit in Lilongwe, Malawi, was reviewed over the first 18 months. 28. Tenthani et al. (2014): Retention in care under universal antiretroviral therapy for HIV-infected pregnant and breastfeeding women (Option B+) in Malawi was analyzed. 29. Thistle et al. (2011): The feasibility of PMTCT using highly active antiretroviral therapy during a socio-economic crisis in rural Zimbabwe was demonstrated. 30. Thomas et al. (2011): The Kisumu Breastfeeding Study in Kenya evaluated triple-antiretroviral prophylaxis to prevent MTCT of HIV through breastfeeding. 31. Tweya et al. (2014): Factors contributing to loss to follow-up among women in the Option B+ PMTCT program in Lilongwe, Malawi, were explored. 32. UNAIDS (2012, 2013, 2014): Global reports on the AIDS epidemic and progress on the global plan were published, providing insights into HIV prevention and treatment strategies. 33. UNICEF (2012): Key considerations for implementing equity-focused approaches to eliminate new HIV infections among children and keep mothers living with HIV alive were outlined. 34. van Lettow et al. (2014): Performance of different care models for initiating lifelong antiretroviral therapy for pregnant women in Malawi under Option B+ was evaluated. 35. WHO (2010, 2012, 2013): Guidelines on antiretroviral therapy for HIV infection in adults and adolescents, as well as updates on PMTCT programs, were published. 36. Fonner et al. (2015):
